issues.title: Define how qlog records multipath negotiation and initial path limits.
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Log multipath negotiation through quic:parameters_set  like a typed mapping for `initial_max_path_id` in `quic:parameters_set`. this is so that a trace should make it possible to understand whether multipath was negotiated and which initial limit each endpoint advertised.

Suggested additions:

- Extend `$$quic-parametersset-extension` with `initial_max_path_id`, using the RFC 10069 range of 0 through 4294967295.
- Preserve the base event’s `initiator` semantics so local and remote advertisements can be distinguished.
- Explain that a parameter present on the wire with value `0` still advertises support. Distinguish absence on the wire from a value omitted because the logger did not capture it.
- Include examples for both endpoints advertising support, an advertisement with value `0`, and one endpoint not advertising the parameter.

References: [RFC 10069 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-2), [§2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-2.1), and [qlog QUIC events §5.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14#section-5.3).

comments.author: altanai
comments.body: RFC 10069 prohibits remembering this kind off parameter for use in a subsequent connection. It should not be presented as a valid restored parameter that enables multipath for 0-RTT. This does not prohibit retaining it in diagnostic logs.

issues.title: Define how path validation outcomes are logged
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
The draft explicitly allows `quic:path_created` to be emitted while validation is still pending. A reader therefore needs a defined way to determine when validation succeeds, fails, or is unnecessary because the tuple was previously validated. Advertised `available` or `backup` status expresses a usage preference and does not establish validation success.

Suggested additions:

- Specify how to log validation start, success, and failure for a given Path ID and tuple, including the endpoint’s perspective.
- Explain how existing `quic:migration_state_updated` probing states, `quic:timer_updated` with `path_validation`, and PATH_CHALLENGE/PATH_RESPONSE packet events should be used. Define an additional field or event only if the existing events cannot express the outcome.
- Distinguish establishing an additional path from migrating an existing Path ID to a new tuple. In particular, avoid requiring `migration_complete` for additional-path establishment, since its base semantics include discarding the old path.
- Cover reuse of an already validated tuple, and include success and failure examples showing the relationship to `path_created` and `path_abandoned`.

References: [RFC 10069 §3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-3.1), [qlog QUIC events §5.21](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14#section-5.21), and [§5.22](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14#section-5.22).

Related: #5.

issues.title: Make event-level path_id requirements machine-checkable
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
So far the draft says certain events need a path_id, and that it must be an unsigned 32-bit number. But declaring that field on its own doesn’t show a validator how to check a complete event or which event types require it. Hence I suggest we provide 
-  schema composition, validation profile, or validation guidance connecting `MultipathEventFields` to the complete events to which it applies.
- Clarify which requirements are checked by CDDL and which require semantic checks, such as whether an event describes one known path or connection-wide state.
- Demonstrate that the field appears alongside `time`, `name`, and `data`, with the correct unsigned 32-bit range.
- Include valid boundary examples (`0` and `4294967295`) and invalid examples (negative values, `4294967296`, a missing required field, and a field incorrectly placed inside `data`).
- Account for the permitted use of `common_fields` when validating the effective field value.
- Add a reproducible check for the combined main, QUIC, and multipath schemas and these examples; document the semantic checks separately where needed.

References: [qlog main schema §7](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-main-schema-15#section-7) and [§8.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-main-schema-15#section-8.2).

Related: #5.

issues.title: Explain how to correlate 1-RTT packet events by path ID and packet number
issues.author: Yanmei-Liu
issues.body:
A tool such as qvis draws a line from a packet’s send event at one endpoint to its receive event at the peer. With Multipath QUIC, each path has its own Application Data packet number space. A client can send packet 42 on path 0 and another packet 42 on path 1. If the server receives only the second packet, matching on packet number alone can draw a line to the wrong send event. [RFC 10069](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc10069)

The draft should explain that, for a given connection and sending direction, a trace consumer matches 1-RTT packet events using `(path_id, packet_number)`. In the example above, the server’s receive event for `(1, 42)` matches the client’s send event for `(1, 42)`. A loss event for `(0, 42)` refers to the other packet.

Require the event-level `path_id` on every event that reports a specific 1-RTT packet, including `quic:packet_sent`, `quic:packet_received`, and `quic:packet_lost`. This includes 1-RTT packets on path 0.

For Initial, Handshake, 0-RTT, and Retry packets, the path is always 0. Should producers record `path_id: 0` explicitly for these packet types, or may consumers infer it from the packet type? Retry has no packet number, so only the path-labeling question applies to it. [RFC 9000, Section 12.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html#section-12.3)

Related to #3 and #20.

issues.title: Should the path_id be added to the event header or to the event data?
issues.author: huitema
issues.body:
In a chat discussion, @flub pointed out that "in our implementation we had added the path_id mostly to the existing data fields, rather than having it in the event header. I wonder what seems to have motivated everyone else to put it in the event header? Especially since it does not apply to all events. Are there any other header fields that have a precedent for this?"

The current design is based ont he implementation in picoquic, which puts the path_id close to the packet number in the event header. However, that was done before updates to the qlog draft moved the packet number field out of the event header, to the packet header in the data field.

We may need to update the text and do a similar move. It makes sense, because the destination connection ID in the packet header is ties to the path_id, and the packet number belong to a packet number space identified by the packet type and the path_id. However, not all events carry a packet header, so for some events we will need to add the path_id to the event data field.

comments.author: altanai
comments.body: I’m good with using `data.header.path_id` when the event includes a packet header, and `data.path_id` when the event refers to a known path but has no packet header. If there’s no single known path, omit the field. Thoughts ?

comments.author: huitema
comments.body: @altanai if we agree to move the path_id out of the header, that's indeed what we will do. But let's wait for a few more comments before we do that.

comments.author: altanai
comments.body:
sounds good @huitema 
 Original thinking was to put path_id at the top-level of event  so its better accessible  and also it was meant ot be optional. 
If we agree on the split, could we include two packet_lost examples with a known path, one with data.header and one without? Since the packet header is optional, that would show readers exactly where to find path_id in both cases.

comments.author: Yanmei-Liu
comments.body:
I have a different view on where the path ID should go. There are three possible locations for the path ID associated with an event:

- **A — `event.path_id`**: at the top level, alongside `time`, `name`, and `data`.
- **B — `event.data.header.path_id`**: inside the packet header, alongside fields such as `packet_number`.
- **C — `event.data.path_id`**: directly in `data`, alongside `header` when present.

The proposal earlier in this thread combines B and C: use B when the event includes a packet header and C when the header is absent but the path is known.

I lean slightly toward **A**. A single, predictable location gives loggers one place to write the path ID and analysis tools one place to read it. `quic:packet_lost` illustrates the drawback of B: the logger may know which path carried the lost packet even when it omits the optional header. With the B/C split, that logging choice changes where a tool has to look for the same information.

Both A and C provide a stable location. What tips the balance toward A for me is how we use multipath traces: For example, a rise in smoothed RTT or a run of consecutive packet losses on one path can indicate a problem with that path. With a top-level `path_id`, a tool can first group all events for that path into a timeline, then decode the event-specific `data` it needs to investigate.

comments.author: flub
comments.body:
Agree that having a single location makes things easier. Additionally having it in `PacketHeader` might be slightly misleading since this is not really a field in the header, it is rather derived from it. So I don't think I'm a big fan of B.

I find it slightly odd to have a field that does not belong to all events in the toplevel event, like A suggests. For that reason I lean slightly towards C I think. I don't think to filter you need to parse each event-specific data field, filtering can still be done without knowing the specific schema.

comments.author: huitema
comments.body:
Keeping the option names defined by @Yanmei-Liu, it seems that we have the following list of pro and con:

* Option A:
  - Pro: path_id at a single place. It is easy to filter events belonging to a path and analyze that path.
  - Con: not all events have a path ID.
* Option B:
  - Pro: for transmission events, having the path_id close to CID and PN seems natural.
  - Con: the packet header is an optional field.
  - Con: the packet header would mix info in the packet (CID, PN) and info derived from the CID (Path_ID)
* Option C:
  - Pro: the packet header is unchanged
  - Con: filtering per path requires parsing the event data.
  - Con: requires updating event.data syntax for all events.

Based on that, my personal opinion is evolving towards keeping option A for now. Maybe add text somewhere in the draft to discuss the design choice.

comments.author: altanai
comments.body:
righto so I’d stick with option A, the top-level path_id I originally proposed in [PR #3](https://github.com/huitema/qlog-multipath-extension/pull/3). Like we asked it gives tools one place to find the path for packet, recovery, and path management events. For packet_lost, that location stays the same whether or not the logger includes data.header.

There’s precedent in [quicwg/qlog#134](https://github.com/quicwg/qlog/issues/134) where Robin proposed an event-level path identifier so tools like qvis could distinguish paths within a single connection trace. The generic field that came out of that work later became tuple, which is still an optional top-level field. I’d use the same placement for the RFC 10069 Path ID and add a short rationale to the draft like @huitema  suggested

comments.author: huitema
comments.body: Closing this issue and keeping option A for now. The PR #30 has been updated to incorporate a short rationale for the design. We can always revisit the issue if we get feedback once the draft is published.

pulls.title: Define qlog events for multipath path creation, abandonment, and status
pulls.author: Yanmei-Liu
pulls.body:
Closes #6.

Packet events show when a path-management signal was sent or received. These three Base-level events record when the logging endpoint changed its path configuration.

- `quic:path_created` records when the client initiates a path or the server accepts it. Address validation can still be pending.
- `quic:path_abandoned` records the endpoint's first decision to abandon a Path ID, including an unused one. The initiator distinguishes a local decision from one prompted by the peer.
- `quic:path_status_updated` records changes to either endpoint's advertised preference. A status frame can arrive on path 0, set path 1 to backup, and later be repeated. The trace records one update for path 1.

All three events use the affected path's top-level `path_id`, consistent with #3. The draft supplies the CDDL data definitions, a client-side example, and the IANA event list. The schema URI uses the `#multipath` fragment prescribed for an extension of the `quic` namespace. [qlog main schema §8](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-main-schema-15#section-8)

The draft built as text and HTML. All three examples validated against their CDDL data types and the combined `$ProtocolEventData` choice. Additional checks covered required fields, status values, and integer limits.

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body: Great start, thanks. Can we make sure that the URN is at the right place, and that the path ID is defined as a 32 bit integer?

comments.body: The URN definition should be in the top section, not in the "draft event" section that will be deleted upon publication!
We do not use varint in qlog. This probably should be an int32.

In aaf0f90, I clarified the definition of `urn:ietf:params:qlog:events:quic#multipath` in the permanent “Event Schema Definition” section. The draft-only subsection now refers back to that definition and explains the version suffix, with `-00` as the example. Could you take another look at the placement?

I removed `QUICPathVarInt` in aaf0f90 and made `path_id` explicit in the CDDL as a required top-level `uint32` on all three events. This covers the full unsigned 32-bit Path ID range in RFC 10069. The `error_code` and `sequence_number` fields can exceed 32 bits, so they use qlog’s `uint64` with the RFC limit of 2^62 − 1. Could you review the updated types and let me know if this addresses your concern?

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body:
Thanks.

Using "quic#multipath" is nice. It seems like the right way to say that we are incrementing the definitions in the QUIC name space.

We may need to revisit some of the definition after discussing with a wider audience, but this is a very good start.

pulls.title: Define qlog representations for RFC 10069 multipath frames
pulls.author: Yanmei-Liu
pulls.body:
Closes #7.

This change extends `$QuicFrame` with qlog representations for every frame in RFC 10069, Table 3. A frame's `path_id` identifies the path named on the wire, which can differ from the path carrying the packet. The packet example shows a PATH_ACK for path 1 and a PATH_CIDS_BLOCKED for path 2 travelling together on path 0.

Both PATH_ACK encodings use the base qlog ACK range and delay conventions. The ECN form carries all three counters, including zeros. The definitions also cover per-path status and connection ID sequence numbers, the maximum and blocked Path ID limits, and the named and unknown PATH_ABANDON transport errors. [RFC 10069, Section 4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-4) · [Base qlog frame definitions](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14#section-8.13)

The draft built as text and HTML. Validation combined this CDDL with the published qlog main schema (-15) and QUIC events (-14). All 10 wire type values were covered. The validator accepted 17 valid frame cases and the example packet payload, and rejected 10 invalid cases.

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body: Looks like a very good first version!

pulls.title: Describe per-path congestion control and recovery in qlog
pulls.author: Yanmei-Liu
pulls.body:
Closes #12. Complements the event-level `path_id` proposal in #3.

Specify which path owns a congestion-control metric, RTT estimate, PTO, loss declaration, and retransmission decision. The sender trace shows a PTO probe on path 1, its acknowledgment arriving on path 0, and the lost stream bytes being sent again on path 0. Both data packets have number 42, so the example also shows why the sending path is needed to identify a packet.

The only proposed new data field is the optional `path_state_discarded: true` on `quic:packet_lost`. It identifies packets first declared lost when the endpoint discards an abandoned path’s state. [RFC 10069 §3.4.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-3.4.3)

Built the text and HTML draft with xml2rfc. Checked the nine example events, validated their payloads and frame objects against the combined qlog CDDL, and tested the new field's presence, omission, and invalid values.

pulls.title: Log the initial_max_path_id transport parameter in parameters_set
pulls.author: mp0rta
pulls.body:
The draft covers the RFC 10069 frames and path events, but not the `initial_max_path_id` transport parameter ([RFC 10069 §2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-2.1)).

This adds it as an optional `uint32` field of the existing `quic:parameters_set` event, through `$$quic-parametersset-extension`. `quic:parameters_restored` is not changed, since the parameter is not remembered for a subsequent connection.

The draft built as text and HTML. The example validated against the combined qlog CDDL. For the new field, 0 and 2^32-1 were accepted; a text value, 2^32 and -1 were rejected.

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body: Thanks for the input, @mp0rta. Yes, we need to add a new value in the parameters list, and also make sure that all implementations use the same string to identify it.

pulls.title: Add machine-checkable path_id validation
pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body:
intended for the issue #20.

Add a CDDL overlay that constrains `path_id` on complete qlog events and trace common fields while preserving the main and QUIC event schemas. Include semantic validation cases for unsigned 32-bit boundaries, common-field inheritance and consistency, missing IDs for known path context, and invalid placement inside `data`.

The overlay is meant to be compiled in the same CDDL unit as the qlog main schema, QUIC event schema, and multipath schema. The Python checker covers semantic rules CDDL cannot express.

Validation: `python3 scripts/check_path_id_validation.py` — 10 cases passed.

pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body: Add `quic:path_validation_updated` to report local path validation transitions, including optional trigger, failure reason, and PATH_ABANDON error code. Register the event type alongside the existing multipath path lifecycle events.

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body:
I am not sure about that one. The validation really is by tuple, not by path. We already have a "migration state updated" event in the main QUIC schema:

[5.21. ](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events.html#section-5.21)[migration_state_updated](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events.html#name-migration_state_updated)

Validation is not listed per se, but it is pretty much the same as "migration_complete".

reviews.author: Yanmei-Liu
reviews.body: Thank you for making the local endpoint’s validation outcome explicit. I’ve left three inline suggestions on identifying the tuple, keeping the CDDL parseable, and interpreting the outcome.

comments.body: Could we log the `tuple` being validated alongside `path_id`? Migration can change the tuple under one Path ID, and a new Path ID can reuse a validated tuple. `migration_complete` implies the old path was discarded, but it can stay active when an additional path is validated. [RFC 10069 §3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-3.1), [§3.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-3.1.2), [qlog §5.21](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14#section-5.21).

CDDL allows only one rule name to the left of `=`. `QUICPathValidationUpdated` already has its own definition above. [RFC 8610, Appendix B](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8610.html#appendix-B).

```suggestion
QUICPathStatusUpdated = {
```

Could `succeeded` require receiving a matching `PATH_RESPONSE`, and `failed` mean the endpoint gave up an outstanding validation attempt? A match can validate the address while the 1200-byte MTU check is still pending. `PATH_ABANDON` can close an unused Path ID, so its error code alone says why the path closed. [RFC 9000 §8.2.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html#section-8.2.3), [§8.2.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html#section-8.2.4), [RFC 10069 §3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-3.1), [§3.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-3.4), [§4.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-4.2.1).

We usually say "initiated". But we really should not attach this to the path. This is a tuple event.

pulls.title: Explain how to correlate 1-RTT packets across paths
pulls.author: Yanmei-Liu
pulls.body:
Closes #24.

Within one connection and sending direction, match 1-RTT qlog events by `(path_id, packet_number)`. Include the event-level `path_id` even on path 0. [RFC 10069 §1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-1)

In the example, the server's receive event matches the client's send of `(1, 42)`. The client's loss event matches its send of `(0, 42)`.

Record `path_id: 0` for Initial, Handshake, 0-RTT, and Retry packet events. Omit `packet_number` for Retry. [RFC 9000 §12.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html#section-12.3)

Rendered the draft as text and HTML, validated the four example events against the qlog and multipath CDDL, and checked both packet matches.

comments.body:
The last line is not necessary. The syntax in the QUIC events draft says:
~~~
    ; only if packet_type === "initial" || "handshake" || "0RTT" ||
    ;                         "1RTT"
    ? packet_number_length: uint8
~~~
We don't need to repeat that there is no packet number for Retry. Or for Version Negotiation.

```suggestion
The `path_id` is set to 0 for Initial, Handshake, 0-RTT, and Retry packet events.
```

pulls.title: Clarify how qlog records multipath negotiation
pulls.author: Yanmei-Liu
pulls.body:
Closes #18.

In `quic:parameters_set`, the optional `initial_max_path_id` field records the value advertised by the endpoint identified by `initiator`. The draft now points directly to [Section 2.1 of RFC 10069](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10069.html#section-2.1) for the transport parameter definition.

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body: No, we should not do that. The "multipath" log extension should just say how variables are logged, and which element of RFC 10069 they represent. Maybe add a pointer to the section of 10069 where this is described, but do not repeat or paraphrase the text.

comments.body: I don't think we should have that level of detail. Your text is repeating the content of RFC 10029, and we should not do that. The text that it replaces was falling in the same trap. It would be sufficient to say that `initial_max_path_id: uint32` records the content of the `initial_max_path_id` TP sent by the initiator, and is only present if the TP was advertised by the initiator.
I’ve removed the redundant text.

reviews.author: huitema
reviews.body: Yes. Good example of focusing on the essential!

Could we scope this example to 1-RTT packets in one connection and sending direction? Packet numbers can repeat across number spaces, and PATH_ACK identifies the path on which the acknowledged packet was sent.
Section 4 says “top-level `Event` map,” while Section 5 says “event headers.” Once #31 settles where `path_id` belongs, could we use the same terminology in both sections?

Yes, we need to a be a bit more formal here. The definition in the [main draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-quic-qlog-main-schema-15) is for an "Event Class", defined as:

```
Event = {
    time: float64
    name: text
    data: $ProtocolEventData
    ? tuple: TupleID
    ? time_format: TimeFormat
    ? group_id: GroupID
    ? system_info: SystemInformation

    ; events can contain any amount of custom fields
    * text => any
}
```

There is no such thing as an event header. There is an event class, with a definition to which we could add:
```
    ? path_id: PathID
```
This extension would apply to concrete events defined in the QUIC extension.


pulls.title: Copy security section from QLOG-QUIC.
pulls.author: huitema
pulls.body:
I looked at the security sections of QLOG-MAIN and QLOG-QUIC. The text proposed here is a direct copy of the text in QLOG-QUIC, which points to QLOG-MAIN. The text in QLOG-MAIN is well developed, and I think is sufficient for now. If we later find threats specific to multipath logging, we can always update the section.

Fixes #9
